# Masses

Moved from the root `CLAUDE.md`, word for word: the root keeps the rules and the map, and this file is read when the area is touched.

A mass (`Mass`, category `mass`) is a footprint (`Mass::footprint`: counter-clockwise whichever way `boundary` runs) extruded from
`base_offset` over `level` up to `top_level` or `height`, as a shaft is, with `params`. Given a `top` outline (as many points as
`boundary`, twin for twin, and running the same way round; `Mass::top_ring` has it counter-clockwise like the footprint) it is lofted
straight between the two (`Mass::lofted`: a `top` equal to the footprint is no loft, and the `mass` command drops it; its `lean`
parameter makes `top` by moving the footprint sideways, a sloped mass). `Model::mass_outline(ms, z)` is the cross section at a height,
the footprint, or each corner that far along its way to its twin (`massing::ring_at`), and everything that measures a mass asks it:
floors, the `massfloor` and `mass` schedules, gross floor area, the plan, snaps. The area is a quadratic of the height, so
`Model::mass_volume` is Simpson's rule on three cross sections, exact. `massing::loft_problem` (which `Model::check` and the IFC import
both ask) refuses a top outline that doesn't pair up, runs the other way round, or collapses the cross section at some sixteenth of
the way up. A plan dashes the outline at its cut height where the plane passes through it (`Model::mass_cut_by`); a section outlines
where its line cuts it and never fills it in poché (`section` leaves masses out of `cuts`; a straight one's stretches come from
`view3d::crossings`, a lofted one's lines from `massing::section_lines`, the cut of its skin of triangles, joined end to end); 3D draws
a straight one as a slab and a lofted one as `massing::tris`, a closed skin turned out (two triangles on a side whose twin
edges are parallel, which makes it flat; a side that twists is cut into `massing::STRIPS` strips up its height, so a twisted loft's volume
in 3D and IFC is a percent or two under the exact one, while the areas and volumes the model reports are exact),
see-through by `graphics::MASS_TRANSPARENCY` unless the view's graphics say otherwise (`Look::with` starts a mass's override there, so a
project with masses never takes its plain shortcut). Show Mass (`show_mass`, MH) is `graphics {hide|show: [mass]}` on one view.
`Model::mass_slices` is the levels it crosses, from its base up to, not including, its top, each with how far the mass goes up from
there: `mass_floors` and the rows of the `massfloor` schedule (`schedule::sources`; a `Row` carries the schedule's category, not its
element's) come from it.
What a mass makes remembers it, under reserved names in `params` as phases and paint are held (`massing.rs`; no project or family
parameter may take them, `Model::check` holds each to a real mass and a level or a face of the right kind, `delete` takes off the marks
naming a mass that goes, and a copy or a split piece loses its own). `mass_floors` leaves `Mass Floor`, `{mass, level}`, on its floors,
so a second run finds them by it, gives them the mass's outline at their level (and the type, if one is given), makes none again, lists
as `stale` the ones on levels the mass no longer crosses and deletes those only with `prune`. `wall_by_face`, `floor_by_face` and
`roof_by_face` build their element by running `wall`, `floor` and `roof` with the face's parameters, so those commands' checks stay the
one place, and leave `Mass Face`, `{mass, face}`: an edge number (numbered from the first point, counter-clockwise) for a wall, `"top"`
for a floor or a roof. A wall stands plumb, so only on a face whose top edge is right over its bottom edge (`massing::plumb`); a floor
and a roof lie on the top outline. `update_by_face` (UF; Revit's Update to Face has no default shortcut) rebuilds the geometry of the
ones asked for, a mass's, or all of them (`massing::follow`: a wall's ends, level, offset and height or top level; a floor's or roof's
boundary, level and offset; the type, a roof's slope and the rest stay) and refuses the lot, naming each, when a face is gone. A mass
mirrored in place runs its outline round the other way, so `relocate` renumbers the faces its walls hold (`massing::mirrored`). Nothing
else ties them to the mass, and IFC carries no mark: what comes back from a file is ordinary. `commands::category` reads `mass` and
`masses` as `mass` (it trims every trailing `s`, which would make `ma`). IFC writes a mass as an `IFCBUILDINGELEMENTPROXY` of object type
`Mass`, its footprint swept up; a lofted one is a closed `IFCTRIANGULATEDFACESET` with a `BIMCraft_Mass` property set (`ifc::LOFT`) whose
`Loft` says as JSON how the footprint and the top outline pair up, since a face set doesn't. Import reads those before the proxies that
become components of families, and takes a lofted one only when that set's outlines are the body's bottom and its top; a mass whose
outline changes from base to top with no such set is left out and listed. The desktop's Massing tab has the Mass tool (`Tool::Mass`:
corners clicked, Enter or the first corner again finishes, `finish_mass`), Show Mass (the button is pressed while the view shows
masses) and, for each selected mass, the Model by Face buttons, which run the face commands, and Update to Face; a mass's Properties
hold its levels and offsets and `Top Outline`, its corners as `x, y` parted by `;`, blank for none.

# Shape editing for floors and flat roofs: design

This is the plan for IDEAS **MOD-16**: points and split lines on the top of a floor or a flat roof, so one element can fall
to drains, carry cross-falls, ridges and valleys, and keep a flat structure under a screed that tapers. It is what a
terrace, a roof garden, a podium's paving, a shower floor or a car park deck needs, and what BIMCraft can't model today:
each floor is level or one sloped plane, and nothing else. The rules in [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) apply to all of it
(everything is a command, `Model::check` validates, the core has no UI, test first, clean room).

Status, on the branch `mod-16-shape-editing` (raised upstream as IPedrax/BIMCraft#183):

- **Phase 0**, the triangulation, is built (`crates/core/src/triangulation.rs`).
- **Phase 1**, shapes on floors, is built (`crates/core/src/shape_tests.rs`, and
  [levels, walls and roofs](areas/levels-walls-roofs.md) says how): the data and parts, the four commands, the checks,
  `floor_faces` and `shape_planes`, 3D, plans, sections, IFC (one closed faceted Brep per slab, `Model::shape_solid`,
  with `GrossVolume` and `NetVolume`), `volume_m3` in a floor's details, attached walls, transforms, `edit_boundary`,
  snaps and file format 13 (12 when written; upstream took 12 meanwhile). IfcOpenShell validates it with `express_rules=True` (`ci/ifc-coverage.txt` has a shaped
  floor) and measures the slab's volume as BIMCraft gives it.
- **Phase 2**, the variable layer, is built: `Layer::variable`, one a floor or roof type; a shaped floor's level underside
  (`Model::floor_under`) and prisms (`floor_prisms`); its layers in the 3D view and sections (`Variable::bounds`); its
  volume (`floor_volume`, and IFC's from its closed solid); attached walls under it; `Model::check` refusing a point that
  leaves the variable layer thinner than nothing; and reinforcement keeping to the structure under it.
- **Phase 3**, the desktop, is built: Shape Editing's Modify Sub Elements (a point, a corner, or both ends of an edge
  picked, `Floor::shape_pick`, set to the Options Bar's Elevation in one `edit_shape`), Add Point (Elevation, and
  Absolute), Add Split Line and Reset Shape, and a Variable box for a floor's or a roof's layers in Type Properties
  (`crates/ui-egui`; tests `shape_editing_raises_points_draws_split_lines_and_resets_a_floor` and
  `modify_sub_elements_sets_a_points_height_or_an_edges_both_ends`). While a Shape Editing tool is on, each point's height
  is labelled beside it in plan, as the Elevation reads it (`Model::shape_labels`); under Modify Sub Elements each point
  has a grip, and a drag moves it in plan at its height, the split lines ending there with it, in one `edit_shape`
  (`Shape::point_near`, `Shape::moved`; test `modify_sub_elements_drags_a_point_with_its_split_lines_and_labels_its_height`).
  Absolute is above the floor's level for every tool (`absolute_elevations_are_above_the_floors_level_on_any_level`).
  The 3D view edits it too (`orbit.rs`, `shape.rs`): with a Shape Editing tool, each point and corner of the selected
  floor has a grip where its top is, and a drag raises or lowers it to the millimetre (`Camera::along`); a click picks as
  in plan, in pixels (`view3d::shape_pick_3d`), and Add Point and Add Split Line land on the top under the cursor
  (`Camera::on_slope`, `view3d::on_floor_top`), or on a point or corner within reach (tests in
  `crates/ui-egui/src/tests/shape3d.rs`). While a grip is held, in plan or in 3D, the creases the release will leave are
  drawn over the floor (`BimApp::shape_preview`, `Model::shape_creases`, `Shape::raised`; tests
  `a_shape_points_grip_held_mid_drag_previews_where_it_and_its_creases_will_go` and
  `in_3d_a_grip_held_mid_drag_previews_the_creases_its_release_will_leave`). In both views a grip lights up under the
  cursor, a point's height label is a button that turns into a field to type its height in (`BimApp::shape_label`;
  Enter sets it as the Options Bar's Elevation reads it, Esc keeps it, and a click on a label is never the tool's), and
  Add Point and Add Split Line snap onto the shape's points and corners, else onto the nearest edge (outline, openings,
  split lines, creases), the edge lit (`view3d::shape_snap_plan`, `shape_snap_3d`; tests
  `a_points_height_label_clicked_*`, `in_plan_add_point_snaps_*`, `in_3d_add_point_snaps_*`). Modify Sub Elements works
  as Revit's: a click selects a point, a corner or an edge (Shift or Ctrl adds; `shape::Sub`), the Options Bar's
  Elevation then reads its height (blank for none or mixed) and Enter sets it, an edge's both ends; the selection's label
  types it too, an edge's at its middle with ▲/▼ in 3D that drag all of it (`shape_raise_all`); Delete takes selected
  points and split lines off (`shape_delete`). Edit mode colours as Revit's (`shape::draw_marks`): points on an edge green,
  inner ones blue, the outline's and openings' edges dashed green, split lines blue, generated creases grey (tests
  `modify_sub_elements_selects_then_sets_*`, `in_3d_a_picked_edges_arrow_*`). Add Point has Revit's two modes on the
  Options Bar: Along Surface (the default), an offset over the top as it is there now (`add_point`'s `offset`), so a
  point on a part that already slopes stays on it; or Absolute, an elevation above the floor's level. While Add Point or
  Add Split Line is on, the cursor reads how high above the level a click would land (`BimApp::landing_height`; tests
  `add_point_with_an_offset_*`, `add_point_along_the_surface_*`). Both tools' Elevation Base says what elevations
  count from (`shape::Base`): the top as it would be without the shape, the floor's level, or the project's zero, Revit's
  Internal Origin (its Project Base Point and Survey Point wait for shared coordinates); test
  `elevations_read_from_the_elevation_base_*`. Add Point and Add Split Line snap, by priority, to the shape's points and
  corners, an edge's middle, else the nearest point along an edge (`view3d::ShapeSnap`), each with the plan's marker in both
  views: an intersection is always one of its points, its edges being one triangulation's. In 3D a selected point is
  dimensioned plumb from where the top would be without the shape (`in_3d_a_selected_point_is_dimensioned_*`).
  Modify Sub Elements picks folding lines too, Revit's name for the creases no split line makes (`Model::shape_folds`,
  `view3d::shape_pick_plan`, `shape_pick_3d`), and Convert Lines makes the selected ones split lines, one way, as Revit's
  does (`SlabShapeEditor.CreateCreasesFromFoldingLines` in its API); tests `a_shapes_folding_lines_*`,
  `convert_lines_makes_a_selected_folding_line_a_split_line`.
- **Phase 4**, flat roofs, is built: a flat roof by footprint takes a shape through the same commands and tools
  (`Model::shapeable` sees its top as a floor's, `Model::roof_as_floor`), its underside following its top plumb
  (`roof_faces`, `roof_rise`), walls attached under it following its falls, its plan creases thin, its points snapped,
  kept by `edit_boundary` and carried by moves and mirrors; a pitched, extruded or joining roof refuses one, saying why
  (`Roof::unshapeable`). `ci/ifc-coverage.txt` has one for IfcOpenShell. Tests: the three `*roof*` tests in
  `shape_tests.rs`, and `a_flat_roof_by_footprint_is_shaped_as_a_floor_is_and_a_pitched_one_isnt` in the desktop's
  `tests/shape3d.rs`. A roof type's variable layer keeps a shaped roof's underside level at its base, as a floor's does
  (`Model::roof_under`, `roof_prisms`, `roof_solid`, `variable_under`): 3D layers, sections, attached walls, IFC (one
  closed Brep; `ci/ifc-coverage.txt` has both kinds) and the check (tests `a_roofs_variable_layer_*`,
  `a_section_shows_a_roofs_insulation_*`, `a_roof_point_that_would_leave_its_insulation_*`).
- **Phase 5**, the extras, is built:
  - **`falls`** (`crates/core/src/falls.rs`): a floor's or flat roof's shape from its drains and the least fall. Each
    drain takes the part of the outline nearer it than any other; where two parts meet a ridge runs at the top's height;
    from each drain a valley runs to each corner of its part; each drain goes down as far as the fall takes its farthest
    corner, to the tenth of a millimetre down. Every plane then falls at least as asked toward a drain, its lowest corner,
    and so does every valley. Round an opening, a valley runs from the drain round the opening's corners by the shortest
    way, each corner on the cone falling from the drain at the fall, so water reaching it runs on down. `ridges` drawn
    (each from the outline, an opening or another ridge to another) split the top into parts first, each needing a drain.
    The command checks every plane falls as asked to a drain or an opening's corner, and refuses, saying where, what
    doesn't. Refused too: a drain outside or in an opening, two within a millimetre, a corner a drain can reach only over
    the outline or a ridge (an L with one drain: add one on the other wing). Tests `falls_to_two_drains_*`,
    `falls_refuse_*`, `falls_run_round_an_opening_*`, `ridges_drawn_split_the_top_*`.
  - **IFC import of a slab whose top isn't one plane** (`import::shaped_top`): a level floor at its highest point, its
    upward faces' outline, each of their corners under that height (or inside) a point, and each edge two of them share at
    an angle a split line; as thick as it is under its highest corner. What doesn't fold into planes, or folds into others
    than its faces (a step), comes in as before. A roof's body read the same way comes in as a shaped flat roof, unless its
    footprint and pitch already make every corner of its top (a pitched roof stays pitched; an extruded one is read by its
    profile). A variable layer goes out with `Description` `'Variable'` and comes back marked; from a file that says
    nothing, a shaped slab whose underside is level gets its insulation nearest the top, else its substrate, marked
    variable. Tests `a_shaped_slab_exported_and_imported_*`, `a_shaped_floor_over_a_variable_layer_comes_back_*`,
    `a_shaped_flat_roof_comes_back_from_ifc_*`.
  - **Spot Slope** (`spot_slope`, `Spot::slope`, `Model::spot_slope`, `top_plane_at`): in a plan, an arrow downhill from
    the point clicked on a floor or a roof, with how steeply its top falls there, following it; Annotate > Dimension's
    Spot Slope places one. Tests `a_spot_slope_reads_*` and the desktop's
    `spot_slope_reads_the_fall_of_a_shaped_floor_where_its_clicked`.

Line numbers are as of `0733fd4`.

## What users expect

The workflow architects know from the established tools, in our own words:

- A floor (or a roof with no sloped edges) gets **points** on its top. Each point has a height relative to the top the
  element would have without them. The corners of the outline are points too, at 0 until raised or lowered.
- **Split lines** cross the top between two points. They are creases the surface must fold along, so the user decides
  where a ridge or a valley runs instead of leaving it to the triangulation.
- The surface between the points and lines is **flat triangles**. The tool picks the creases it needs and draws them
  apart from the user's own.
- A layer of the type can be **variable**. Then the bottom of the element stays flat and that layer takes up the
  difference: the screed tapers, the concrete under it doesn't. With no variable layer, the whole slab follows its top
  at its type's thickness.
- **Reset Shape** takes it all off again.

## What BIMCraft has today

| What | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| A floor's top is one plane: level, or through the slope arrow's tail rising `slope` degrees | `Model::floor_top`, `model.rs:3737` | `walls::Plane` is `z + g·p`, one gradient |
| A floor's slabs: its outline less its openings, lifted onto that plane, with a uniform `rise` | `Model::floor_slabs`, `model.rs:3755`; `floor_depth`, `model.rs:3749` | thickness is square to the slope, so plumb it's thicker |
| A roof's top is already **many planes**: `roof_faces` gives `(rings, Plane)` per slope | `model.rs:3575`, `roof_pieces` `3727`, `roof_slabs` `3722` | the shape we need, already used by the 3D view, walls and IFC |
| Layers: `function`, `material`, `thickness`; no variable flag | `Layer`, `model.rs:327`; `FloorType` `1886`, `RoofType` `1944` | |
| Triangulation: ear clipping of one simple ring, no holes, no inner points, no constraints | `geom::triangulate`, `geom.rs:153` | not enough for this |
| Faces of an arrangement of segments | `geom::faces`, `geom.rs:263` | useful to check split lines |
| A prism between two planes, cut by sections | `Solid::Prism { ring, bottom, top }`, `view3d.rs:159` | used by walls, ramps, runs |
| IFC: a prism between two planes as a shell | `Step::prism` and `Step::shell`, `ifc.rs:409`, `456` | used by ramps and walls |
| Walls attached to a floor follow one plane over its outline | `Bound::of`, `walls.rs:443` | the roof branch above it already follows many planes |
| IFC import of a slab whose top isn't one plane | `import.rs:1642`, `top_of` `273` | left out ("its top isn't flat"), or read as the plane of its largest upward face |
| Revit import of a sloped or stepped floor | `crates/rvt/src/floors.rs:206` | comes in level, with a note |
| File format | `FORMAT = 11`, `model.rs:90` | |

**The key point:** roofs already prove the pipeline can carry a top made of several planes. The work is to give floors
(and flat roofs) a top made of triangles, then let each consumer read "a list of planar pieces" where it reads "one plane"
today.

## The approach: a top made of planar pieces

One new query gives every consumer what it needs:

```rust
/// A floor's top as planar pieces in plan, each with its plane: one piece for a level or sloped floor,
/// the triangles of its shape (coplanar neighbours merged) for a shaped one.
pub fn floor_faces(&self, f: &Floor) -> Vec<(Vec<P2>, walls::Plane)>
```

`floor_top` stays for the unshaped case and as the reference the point heights are measured from. `floor_slabs` is
rebuilt on `floor_faces`. For a roof, `roof_faces` gains the same branch for a shaped flat roof, so `roof_pieces`,
`roof_slabs` and everything downstream work as they do for slopes.

### Data

```rust
/// Points and split lines on a floor's or a flat roof's top (IDEAS MOD-16).
pub struct Shape {
    pub points: Vec<ShapePoint>,
    pub lines: Vec<SplitLine>,
}

/// A point on the top, `z` mm above (negative: below) where the top would be without the shape.
pub struct ShapePoint { pub id: Id, pub guid: Guid, pub at: P2, pub z: f64 }

/// A crease the top folds along, between two of the shape's points or outline corners.
pub struct SplitLine { pub id: Id, pub guid: Guid, pub a: P2, pub b: P2 }
```

- `Floor` and `Roof` get `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Shape::is_empty")] pub shape: Shape`.
- `ShapePoint` and `SplitLine` are **parts** (`HasPart`, listed in `parts_now`, `sync_parts`, `forget_parts`), as sketch
  lines are, so a schedule, an agent or a later "edit this point" can name one by id.
- Heights are **relative** to the unshaped top, so changing the floor's `offset` moves the whole shape with it. Commands
  may take `absolute: true` and convert when they run.
- A corner of the outline (or of an opening) not listed among the points is at 0. A point may lie on an outline edge,
  where it adds a corner.
- Every end of a split line is one of the points or an outline corner. A command that adds a line with a loose end adds
  that end as a point, at the height the top has there at the time.
- `Layer` gets `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Not::not")] pub variable: bool`.
- **File format 13** (upstream's 12 came first), with a no-op step in `Model::migrate`. An older build that read a shaped floor would drop the shape
  and draw it flat. That's a misreading, not a field it can do without, so the bump is needed (CLAUDE.md, "A file is read
  kindly").

### Geometry

1. **Triangulate in plan:** a constrained Delaunay triangulation of the outline and its openings. The constraints are the
   outline edges, the opening edges and the split lines; the points are the inner vertices. Delaunay makes the result
   deterministic: the same points always give the same creases. Ties between cocircular points are broken by the
   corners' order, x and then y.
2. **Lift:** each vertex's z is the unshaped top there plus its point's `z`.
3. **Merge:** neighbouring triangles whose planes agree (within 0.01 mm at the shared vertices) merge into one polygon.
   A floor with points all at 0 is still one piece, and plans and IFC don't fill with needless diagonals.
4. **Thickness is plumb** for a shaped element: the type's thickness measured vertically, not square to each facet.
   Facets of different pitch then meet without gaps or overlaps underneath. At drainage falls of 1–2 % the difference is
   under 0.03 %. Sloped floors without a shape keep today's rule.
5. **With a variable layer**, the bottom is flat: the unshaped top less the type's thickness. Layers above the variable
   one follow the top, layers below it follow the bottom, and the variable layer is whatever is left at each point. Each
   facet becomes a `Solid::Prism` between its top plane and the flat bottom, not a `Solid::Slab` with a uniform rise.
6. **Caps:** `MAX_SHAPE_POINTS` (2,000) and `MAX_SPLIT_LINES` (2,000); every `z` within `MAX_COORD`. A triangulation
   past the cap is refused with the count, never truncated.

**The triangulation (built, phase 0).** The codebase writes its own geometry (the straight skeleton, the sketch solver,
CSG), its lints forbid panics, and the 3D view and plans run outside `Session::execute`'s `catch_unwind`, so a panic in
a dependency there would take the window down. So it is written here rather than taken from a crate such as `spade`:
`triangulation::constrained(outline, holes, points, lines)`, about 500 lines and 350 of tests.

- **Corners:** those within `TOL` of each other become one, the first in order of x and then y. An edge is cut at any
  corner within `TOL` of it, so a point on the outline bends it there.
- **Exact:** whether a corner lies left of a line, or inside a circle, is worked out in whole numbers on a 0.01 mm grid
  (`i128`), so a nearly flat triangle can't come out the wrong way round. That bounds a region to `MAX_ACROSS`, 10 km,
  well inside the 19 km where the in-circle sum would no longer fit.
- **Steps:** a sweep west to east triangulates the corners' convex hull; Lawson's flips make it Delaunay; Sloan's flips
  bring in each missing edge of the outline, the holes and the lines; Lawson's flips again, never across those edges; and
  a walk in from the hull, changing between outside and inside at each outline or hole edge, keeps the region's
  triangles.
- **Same answer in any order:** the output's corners and triangles are in a fixed order, so the same input in any
  order, either way round, gives an equal `Triangulation`.
- **Refused, saying why:** more than `MAX_CORNERS` (20,000) corners; a point not finite or past `MAX_COORD`; a region
  more than 10 km across; an outline or a hole with no area; a hole outside the outline or over another; a point or a
  line outside the outline or in a hole; a line shorter than a millimetre; edges that cross. Past 20 million flips it
  gives up rather than hold a command.
- **Speed:** 2,000 points with two lines in an L with a hole: about 17 ms, in the test build (the core is optimised
  there too).
- **Tests:** in the module. A random sweep of 400 cases, at least 100 of which must come out, checks that every triangle
  turns counter-clockwise, that they cover the region, and that no edge crosses a line. Leaving out the last Lawson pass
  or Sloan's flips each fails tests.

## Commands

The ids follow the established tool names, as the codebase does elsewhere.

| Command | Params | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `edit_shape` | `{id, points?: [{at, z, id?}], lines?: [{a, b, id?}], absolute?}` | Replaces the shape all at once, as `edit_boundary` does a sketch: what is sent back with an `id` keeps it. Without `points` or `lines`, it replies with the shape as it is: the points, including the corners with their heights; the split lines; the generated creases; and the pieces with their planes. That reply is what agents need to reason about falls. |
| `add_point` | `{id, at, z?, absolute?}` | One point; `z` defaults to the top's height there now (0 relative). |
| `add_split_line` | `{id, a, b}` | One line; loose ends become points at the current height. |
| `reset_shape` | `{id}` | Removes the shape. |
| `type` (floor, roof) | layers take `variable: true` | At most one per type; not on walls or ceilings. |
| `modify` (floor) | unchanged | Rejects `slope` or `arrow` on a shaped floor, with the reason (see Validation). |
| `falls` (phase 5) | `{id, drains: [[x, y], …], fall: 1.5, ridges?: [[[x, y], [x, y]], …]}` | Better than the established tools: sets point heights so water runs to the drains at no less than `fall` %, adding split lines along the valleys. Agents and architects describe a terrace this way, not point by point. |

Every reply lists the pieces' count and the lowest and highest point of the top. `inspect` on a floor already reports
`top: [lo, hi]` (`commands.rs:2122`); it must take the shape's points into account, not only the outline's.

## Validation (`Model::check`)

New rules, each with an error that says what to fix:

- A point outside the outline, or inside an opening: "point 100231 at (12500, 3400) is outside floor 100190: move it inside, or delete it".
- A split line that crosses another, crosses an opening, or leaves the outline (reuse `sketch::solve`'s problem kinds and wording).
- A split line end that is neither a point nor an outline corner.
- Two points within 1 mm of each other.
- A shape on a sloped floor (with `arrow`), or on a roof that isn't by footprint with `slope` 0. In version 1 the two are
  exclusive: shape a level element, and give its slope through the points.
- More than one variable layer in a type.
- **A variable layer thinner than nothing** anywhere: "at point 100231 the screed would be −12 mm: raise the point by 12
  mm or thicken the variable layer".
- With no variable layer, nothing bounds the depth: the slab just follows the top.

## What changes, consumer by consumer

| Consumer | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `Model::floor_slabs` (`model.rs:3755`) | one plane over the outline less openings | built on `floor_faces`; each piece less the openings |
| `Model::roof_faces` (`model.rs:3575`) | a flat roof is one plane | a shaped flat roof returns its pieces; `roof_rise` is plumb for them |
| 3D solids (`view3d.rs:511`, `612`) | `Solid::Slab` per piece | the same for constant thickness; `Solid::Prism` (top facet, flat bottom) with a variable layer |
| 3D layers (`view3d::layered`, `view3d.rs:741`) | a slab's layers in proportion; the `Prism` branch is walls only | a slab `Prism` branch: layers above the variable one from the top, below it from the bottom |
| Section layers (`render.rs:1230`) | each cut quad split in proportion to the layers' thicknesses | the same rule as 3D: fixed layers measured from the top or the bottom edge, the variable one between |
| Plan (`render.rs:1585`) | outline, openings, surface pattern, slope arrow | the pattern over each piece; split lines solid and generated creases dashed, thin, when the element is selected or being edited; each point's height as a label while editing (built as the desktop's overlay, not in `render.rs`, so it never prints) |
| Attached walls (`walls.rs:454`) | one plane over the floor's convex pieces | each piece with its own plane, as the roof branch above it does |
| Shafts (`Model::less_shafts`, `model.rs:3773`) | per slab face | already per face: no change, but a test |
| Move, copy, rotate, mirror (`commands.rs:8236`) | outline, openings, arrow, pattern | the points' `at` and the lines' ends too; a mirror keeps the heights |
| `edit_boundary` | redraws the outline | keeps the points inside the new outline and its openings, cuts each split line where it leaves the outline or enters an opening (keeping the pieces inside), and puts a point at the height the top had at each new end and each new corner, so the top round a new hole or a moved edge stays as it was; the reply names what was `dropped`, `cut` and `added` (built; test `a_hole_cut_through_a_shape_*`) |
| A floor's details (`element_json`, `commands.rs:2122`) | area and top from the outline | top range over every point; a volume (`volume_m3`) for every floor |
| Reinforce (`reinforce.rs:409`) | bars from `floor_top` | with a variable layer above the structure, the structure is flat: bars from the flat bottom. Otherwise refuse in version 1, saying why |
| IFC export (`ifc.rs:658`) | level: an extruded profile; sloped: per-piece Breps; quantities only `Width` when sloped | a shaped slab is **one closed `IfcFacetedBrep`**: top facets, a flat or following bottom, and plumb sides, all planar. Write `NetVolume` and `GrossVolume` for sloped and shaped slabs too, from the prisms. |
| Snaps (`snap.rs:320`, `603`) | outline edges and corners | the shape's points and split lines too |
| IFC import (`import.rs:1642`) | a top that isn't one plane is left out or forced flat | phase 5: read the upward faces' vertices as points relative to the highest plane, and the creases as split lines |
| Revit import (`crates/rvt/src/floors.rs:206`) | sloped or stepped comes in level | out of scope: reading the slab's shape from `.rvt` is research under the provenance fence |
| `lenient.rs`, `Element::refs_mut`, `parts_now` | | the new fields and parts, as the rules require |

## Desktop (`crates/ui-egui`)

- With a floor, or a flat roof, selected: a **Shape Editing** panel in the contextual tab, next to Slope Arrow
  (`lib.rs:3783`), with Modify Sub Elements, Add Point, Add Split Line and Reset Shape.
- **Add Point:** click on the top. The Options Bar takes the height and an Absolute check box.
- **Add Split Line:** two clicks, snapping to points, corners and edges.
- **Modify Sub Elements:** click a point or an edge (an edge sets both its ends) and type its height. Points drag in plan
  with the usual grips; in the 3D view (`orbit.rs`) their grips, and the corners', drag heights up or down.
- Every action runs a command. The canvas holds no geometry of its own (CLAUDE.md, "The UI is thin").
- egui_kittest tests: place a point at a model point, type −30, and check the reply's top range and the plan's pixels.

## Out of scope

- A different slope on each roof edge (upstream issue #74), and slope arrows on roofs and ceilings: separate items.
- Shaped ceilings; curved (smooth) tops; "pick supports" from beams.
- Toposolids. This work is their engine, though: a toposolid is a floor-like element whose top is a shape, so site and
  paving reuse `Shape`, the triangulation and every consumer change above.
- Reading shaped floors from `.rvt`.

## Phases, sizes and the tests that open each

Sizes as the roadmap gives them, for one developer working with agents.

| Phase | Size | First failing tests |
|---|---|---|
| **0. Triangulation** in `triangulation.rs` (built) | M | A square with a centre point gives 4 triangles; a split line is always an edge; an opening stays empty; the same input in any order gives the same triangles; duplicates, collinear runs, points on edges and the cap never panic (a property sweep). |
| **1. Shape on floors** (built, but for what the status above lists): data, commands, `check`, `floor_faces`, 3D, plan, sections (no variable layer), attached walls, transforms, `edit_boundary`, `inspect`, IFC export, snaps, format 13 | L | A 10 × 10 m floor with a drain at −30 mm gives 4 faces and the volume to 0.1 %; a section through the drain shows a V top; a wall attached under it follows the creases; IfcOpenShell validates the closed Brep with `express_rules=True`; mirror and move keep the shape; a format-12 file opens and a format-13 file is refused by 12; `hostile_params_never_panic_or_break_the_model` covers the new commands as it does every command. |
| **2. Variable layer** | M | A tile, screed (variable), membrane and concrete type: the section shows the concrete flat and the screed tapering; the 3D view's layers match; `check` refuses a point that makes the screed negative; reinforcement follows the flat structure. |
| **3. Desktop** | M | Add Point at a clicked model point with −30 typed; Add Split Line snapping to two corners; Reset Shape; the three looks screenshotted as `docs/areas/looking-at-results.md` asks. |
| **4. Flat roofs** | S | A flat roof by footprint with four drains; walls attached to it; a sloped roof refuses a shape. |
| **5. Extras**: `falls`, IFC import of multi-plane slabs, a spot slope annotation | M | `falls` with two drains gives at least 1.5 % everywhere and every point running to a drain; a shaped slab exported and imported comes back with the same points. |

**About two months in all.** After phases 0–2 (about a month) agents, the CLI and MCP can model falls to drains and
tapering screeds, and IFC carries them. The desktop tools follow.

## Open questions

1. Triangulation: written here (done in phase 0, in its own module rather than `geom`), unless the maintainer would
   rather have `spade`; #183 asks.
2. Shaped thickness plumb (proposed), or square to each facet as sloped floors are today?
3. Shape and slope arrow exclusive in version 1 (proposed), or a shape on top of a sloped plane?
4. Creases: plans draw every plane's edges always, as thin as the outline (built that way, as the simplest start).
   Generated creases dashed apart from the user's split lines, or shown only while selected, could come with the
   desktop tools.
5. Upstream first: IDEAS asks for an issue naming **MOD-16** before the work starts, so the fork doesn't drift from
   `IPedrax/BIMCraft`.

content.content:
# Masses

Moved from the root `CLAUDE.md`, word for word: the root keeps the rules and the map, and this file is read when the area is touched.

A mass (`Mass`, category `mass`) is a footprint (`Mass::footprint`: counter-clockwise whichever way `boundary` runs) extruded from
`base_offset` over `level` up to `top_level` or `height`, as a shaft is, with `params`. Given a `top` outline (as many points as
`boundary`, twin for twin, and running the same way round; `Mass::top_ring` has it counter-clockwise like the footprint) it is lofted
straight between the two (`Mass::lofted`: a `top` equal to the footprint is no loft, and the `mass` command drops it; its `lean`
parameter makes `top` by moving the footprint sideways, a sloped mass). `Model::mass_outline(ms, z)` is the cross section at a height,
the footprint, or each corner that far along its way to its twin (`massing::ring_at`), and everything that measures a mass asks it:
floors, the `massfloor` and `mass` schedules, gross floor area, the plan, snaps. The area is a quadratic of the height, so
`Model::mass_volume` is Simpson's rule on three cross sections, exact. `massing::loft_problem` (which `Model::check` and the IFC import
both ask) refuses a top outline that doesn't pair up, runs the other way round, or collapses the cross section at some sixteenth of
the way up. A plan dashes the outline at its cut height where the plane passes through it (`Model::mass_cut_by`); a section outlines
where its line cuts it and never fills it in poché (`section` leaves masses out of `cuts`; a straight one's stretches come from
`view3d::crossings`, a lofted one's lines from `massing::section_lines`, the cut of its skin of triangles, joined end to end); 3D draws
a straight one as a slab and a lofted one as `massing::tris`, a closed skin turned out (two triangles on a side whose twin
edges are parallel, which makes it flat; a side that twists is cut into `massing::STRIPS` strips up its height, so a twisted loft's volume
in 3D and IFC is a percent or two under the exact one, while the areas and volumes the model reports are exact),
see-through by `graphics::MASS_TRANSPARENCY` unless the view's graphics say otherwise (`Look::with` starts a mass's override there, so a
project with masses never takes its plain shortcut). Show Mass (`show_mass`, MH) is `graphics {hide|show: [mass]}` on one view.
`Model::mass_slices` is the levels it crosses, from its base up to, not including, its top, each with how far the mass goes up from
there: `mass_floors` and the rows of the `massfloor` schedule (`schedule::sources`; a `Row` carries the schedule's category, not its
element's) come from it.
What a mass makes remembers it, under reserved names in `params` as phases and paint are held (`massing.rs`; no project or family
parameter may take them, `Model::check` holds each to a real mass and a level or a face of the right kind, `delete` takes off the marks
naming a mass that goes, and a copy or a split piece loses its own). `mass_floors` leaves `Mass Floor`, `{mass, level}`, on its floors,
so a second run finds them by it, gives them the mass's outline at their level (and the type, if one is given), makes none again, lists
as `stale` the ones on levels the mass no longer crosses and deletes those only with `prune`. `wall_by_face`, `floor_by_face` and
`roof_by_face` build their element by running `wall`, `floor` and `roof` with the face's parameters, so those commands' checks stay the
one place, and leave `Mass Face`, `{mass, face}`: an edge number (numbered from the first point, counter-clockwise) for a wall, `"top"`
for a floor or a roof. A wall stands plumb, so only on a face whose top edge is right over its bottom edge (`massing::plumb`); a floor
and a roof lie on the top outline. `update_by_face` (UF; Revit's Update to Face has no default shortcut) rebuilds the geometry of the
ones asked for, a mass's, or all of them (`massing::follow`: a wall's ends, level, offset and height or top level; a floor's or roof's
boundary, level and offset; the type, a roof's slope and the rest stay) and refuses the lot, naming each, when a face is gone. A mass
mirrored in place runs its outline round the other way, so `relocate` renumbers the faces its walls hold (`massing::mirrored`). Nothing
else ties them to the mass, and IFC carries no mark: what comes back from a file is ordinary. `commands::category` reads `mass` and
`masses` as `mass` (it trims every trailing `s`, which would make `ma`). IFC writes a mass as an `IFCBUILDINGELEMENTPROXY` of object type
`Mass`, its footprint swept up; a lofted one is a closed `IFCTRIANGULATEDFACESET` with a `BIMCraft_Mass` property set (`ifc::LOFT`) whose
`Loft` says as JSON how the footprint and the top outline pair up, since a face set doesn't. Import reads those before the proxies that
become components of families, and takes a lofted one only when that set's outlines are the body's bottom and its top; a mass whose
outline changes from base to top with no such set is left out and listed. The desktop's Massing tab has the Mass tool (`Tool::Mass`:
corners clicked, Enter or the first corner again finishes, `finish_mass`), Show Mass (the button is pressed while the view shows
masses) and, for each selected mass, the Model by Face buttons, which run the face commands, and Update to Face; a mass's Properties
hold its levels and offsets and `Top Outline`, its corners as `x, y` parted by `;`, blank for none.

# Shape editing for floors and flat roofs: design

This is the plan for IDEAS **MOD-16**: points and split lines on the top of a floor or a flat roof, so one element can fall
to drains, carry cross-falls, ridges and valleys, and keep a flat structure under a screed that tapers. It is what a
terrace, a roof garden, a podium's paving, a shower floor or a car park deck needs, and what BIMCraft can't model today:
each floor is level or one sloped plane, and nothing else. The rules in [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) apply to all of it
(everything is a command, `Model::check` validates, the core has no UI, test first, clean room).

Status, on the branch `mod-16-shape-editing` (raised upstream as IPedrax/BIMCraft#183):

- **Phase 0**, the triangulation, is built (`crates/core/src/triangulation.rs`).
- **Phase 1**, shapes on floors, is built (`crates/core/src/shape_tests.rs`, and
  [levels, walls and roofs](areas/levels-walls-roofs.md) says how): the data and parts, the four commands, the checks,
  `floor_faces` and `shape_planes`, 3D, plans, sections, IFC (one closed faceted Brep per slab, `Model::shape_solid`,
  with `GrossVolume` and `NetVolume`), `volume_m3` in a floor's details, attached walls, transforms, `edit_boundary`,
  snaps and file format 13 (12 when written; upstream took 12 meanwhile). IfcOpenShell validates it with `express_rules=True` (`ci/ifc-coverage.txt` has a shaped
  floor) and measures the slab's volume as BIMCraft gives it.
- **Phase 2**, the variable layer, is built: `Layer::variable`, one a floor or roof type; a shaped floor's level underside
  (`Model::floor_under`) and prisms (`floor_prisms`); its layers in the 3D view and sections (`Variable::bounds`); its
  volume (`floor_volume`, and IFC's from its closed solid); attached walls under it; `Model::check` refusing a point that
  leaves the variable layer thinner than nothing; and reinforcement keeping to the structure under it.
- **Phase 3**, the desktop, is built: Shape Editing's Modify Sub Elements (a point, a corner, or both ends of an edge
  picked, `Floor::shape_pick`, set to the Options Bar's Elevation in one `edit_shape`), Add Point (Elevation, and
  Absolute), Add Split Line and Reset Shape, and a Variable box for a floor's or a roof's layers in Type Properties
  (`crates/ui-egui`; tests `shape_editing_raises_points_draws_split_lines_and_resets_a_floor` and
  `modify_sub_elements_sets_a_points_height_or_an_edges_both_ends`). While a Shape Editing tool is on, each point's height
  is labelled beside it in plan, as the Elevation reads it (`Model::shape_labels`); under Modify Sub Elements each point
  has a grip, and a drag moves it in plan at its height, the split lines ending there with it, in one `edit_shape`
  (`Shape::point_near`, `Shape::moved`; test `modify_sub_elements_drags_a_point_with_its_split_lines_and_labels_its_height`).
  Absolute is above the floor's level for every tool (`absolute_elevations_are_above_the_floors_level_on_any_level`).
  The 3D view edits it too (`orbit.rs`, `shape.rs`): with a Shape Editing tool, each point and corner of the selected
  floor has a grip where its top is, and a drag raises or lowers it to the millimetre (`Camera::along`); a click picks as
  in plan, in pixels (`view3d::shape_pick_3d`), and Add Point and Add Split Line land on the top under the cursor
  (`Camera::on_slope`, `view3d::on_floor_top`), or on a point or corner within reach (tests in
  `crates/ui-egui/src/tests/shape3d.rs`). While a grip is held, in plan or in 3D, the creases the release will leave are
  drawn over the floor (`BimApp::shape_preview`, `Model::shape_creases`, `Shape::raised`; tests
  `a_shape_points_grip_held_mid_drag_previews_where_it_and_its_creases_will_go` and
  `in_3d_a_grip_held_mid_drag_previews_the_creases_its_release_will_leave`). In both views a grip lights up under the
  cursor, a point's height label is a button that turns into a field to type its height in (`BimApp::shape_label`;
  Enter sets it as the Options Bar's Elevation reads it, Esc keeps it, and a click on a label is never the tool's), and
  Add Point and Add Split Line snap onto the shape's points and corners, else onto the nearest edge (outline, openings,
  split lines, creases), the edge lit (`view3d::shape_snap_plan`, `shape_snap_3d`; tests
  `a_points_height_label_clicked_*`, `in_plan_add_point_snaps_*`, `in_3d_add_point_snaps_*`). Modify Sub Elements works
  as Revit's: a click selects a point, a corner or an edge (Shift or Ctrl adds; `shape::Sub`), the Options Bar's
  Elevation then reads its height (blank for none or mixed) and Enter sets it, an edge's both ends; the selection's label
  types it too, an edge's at its middle with ▲/▼ in 3D that drag all of it (`shape_raise_all`); Delete takes selected
  points and split lines off (`shape_delete`). Edit mode colours as Revit's (`shape::draw_marks`): points on an edge green,
  inner ones blue, the outline's and openings' edges dashed green, split lines blue, generated creases grey (tests
  `modify_sub_elements_selects_then_sets_*`, `in_3d_a_picked_edges_arrow_*`). Add Point has Revit's two modes on the
  Options Bar: Along Surface (the default), an offset over the top as it is there now (`add_point`'s `offset`), so a
  point on a part that already slopes stays on it; or Absolute, an elevation above the floor's level. While Add Point or
  Add Split Line is on, the cursor reads how high above the level a click would land (`BimApp::landing_height`; tests
  `add_point_with_an_offset_*`, `add_point_along_the_surface_*`). Both tools' Elevation Base says what elevations
  count from (`shape::Base`): the top as it would be without the shape, the floor's level, or the project's zero, Revit's
  Internal Origin (its Project Base Point and Survey Point wait for shared coordinates); test
  `elevations_read_from_the_elevation_base_*`. Add Point and Add Split Line snap, by priority, to the shape's points and
  corners, an edge's middle, else the nearest point along an edge (`view3d::ShapeSnap`), each with the plan's marker in both
  views: an intersection is always one of its points, its edges being one triangulation's. In 3D a selected point is
  dimensioned plumb from where the top would be without the shape (`in_3d_a_selected_point_is_dimensioned_*`).
  Modify Sub Elements picks folding lines too, Revit's name for the creases no split line makes (`Model::shape_folds`,
  `view3d::shape_pick_plan`, `shape_pick_3d`), and Convert Lines makes the selected ones split lines, one way, as Revit's
  does (`SlabShapeEditor.CreateCreasesFromFoldingLines` in its API); tests `a_shapes_folding_lines_*`,
  `convert_lines_makes_a_selected_folding_line_a_split_line`.
- **Phase 4**, flat roofs, is built: a flat roof by footprint takes a shape through the same commands and tools
  (`Model::shapeable` sees its top as a floor's, `Model::roof_as_floor`), its underside following its top plumb
  (`roof_faces`, `roof_rise`), walls attached under it following its falls, its plan creases thin, its points snapped,
  kept by `edit_boundary` and carried by moves and mirrors; a pitched, extruded or joining roof refuses one, saying why
  (`Roof::unshapeable`). `ci/ifc-coverage.txt` has one for IfcOpenShell. Tests: the three `*roof*` tests in
  `shape_tests.rs`, and `a_flat_roof_by_footprint_is_shaped_as_a_floor_is_and_a_pitched_one_isnt` in the desktop's
  `tests/shape3d.rs`. A roof type's variable layer keeps a shaped roof's underside level at its base, as a floor's does
  (`Model::roof_under`, `roof_prisms`, `roof_solid`, `variable_under`): 3D layers, sections, attached walls, IFC (one
  closed Brep; `ci/ifc-coverage.txt` has both kinds) and the check (tests `a_roofs_variable_layer_*`,
  `a_section_shows_a_roofs_insulation_*`, `a_roof_point_that_would_leave_its_insulation_*`).
- **Phase 5**, the extras, is built:
  - **`falls`** (`crates/core/src/falls.rs`): a floor's or flat roof's shape from its drains and the least fall. Each
    drain takes the part of the outline nearer it than any other; where two parts meet a ridge runs at the top's height;
    from each drain a valley runs to each corner of its part; each drain goes down as far as the fall takes its farthest
    corner, to the tenth of a millimetre down. Every plane then falls at least as asked toward a drain, its lowest corner,
    and so does every valley. Round an opening, a valley runs from the drain round the opening's corners by the shortest
    way, each corner on the cone falling from the drain at the fall, so water reaching it runs on down. `ridges` drawn
    (each from the outline, an opening or another ridge to another) split the top into parts first, each needing a drain.
    The command checks every plane falls as asked to a drain or an opening's corner, and refuses, saying where, what
    doesn't. Refused too: a drain outside or in an opening, two within a millimetre, a corner a drain can reach only over
    the outline or a ridge (an L with one drain: add one on the other wing). Tests `falls_to_two_drains_*`,
    `falls_refuse_*`, `falls_run_round_an_opening_*`, `ridges_drawn_split_the_top_*`.
  - **IFC import of a slab whose top isn't one plane** (`import::shaped_top`): a level floor at its highest point, its
    upward faces' outline, each of their corners under that height (or inside) a point, and each edge two of them share at
    an angle a split line; as thick as it is under its highest corner. What doesn't fold into planes, or folds into others
    than its faces (a step), comes in as before. A roof's body read the same way comes in as a shaped flat roof, unless its
    footprint and pitch already make every corner of its top (a pitched roof stays pitched; an extruded one is read by its
    profile). A variable layer goes out with `Description` `'Variable'` and comes back marked; from a file that says
    nothing, a shaped slab whose underside is level gets its insulation nearest the top, else its substrate, marked
    variable. Tests `a_shaped_slab_exported_and_imported_*`, `a_shaped_floor_over_a_variable_layer_comes_back_*`,
    `a_shaped_flat_roof_comes_back_from_ifc_*`.
  - **Spot Slope** (`spot_slope`, `Spot::slope`, `Model::spot_slope`, `top_plane_at`): in a plan, an arrow downhill from
    the point clicked on a floor or a roof, with how steeply its top falls there, following it; Annotate > Dimension's
    Spot Slope places one. Tests `a_spot_slope_reads_*` and the desktop's
    `spot_slope_reads_the_fall_of_a_shaped_floor_where_its_clicked`.

Line numbers are as of `0733fd4`.

## What users expect

The workflow architects know from the established tools, in our own words:

- A floor (or a roof with no sloped edges) gets **points** on its top. Each point has a height relative to the top the
  element would have without them. The corners of the outline are points too, at 0 until raised or lowered.
- **Split lines** cross the top between two points. They are creases the surface must fold along, so the user decides
  where a ridge or a valley runs instead of leaving it to the triangulation.
- The surface between the points and lines is **flat triangles**. The tool picks the creases it needs and draws them
  apart from the user's own.
- A layer of the type can be **variable**. Then the bottom of the element stays flat and that layer takes up the
  difference: the screed tapers, the concrete under it doesn't. With no variable layer, the whole slab follows its top
  at its type's thickness.
- **Reset Shape** takes it all off again.

## What BIMCraft has today

| What | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| A floor's top is one plane: level, or through the slope arrow's tail rising `slope` degrees | `Model::floor_top`, `model.rs:3737` | `walls::Plane` is `z + g·p`, one gradient |
| A floor's slabs: its outline less its openings, lifted onto that plane, with a uniform `rise` | `Model::floor_slabs`, `model.rs:3755`; `floor_depth`, `model.rs:3749` | thickness is square to the slope, so plumb it's thicker |
| A roof's top is already **many planes**: `roof_faces` gives `(rings, Plane)` per slope | `model.rs:3575`, `roof_pieces` `3727`, `roof_slabs` `3722` | the shape we need, already used by the 3D view, walls and IFC |
| Layers: `function`, `material`, `thickness`; no variable flag | `Layer`, `model.rs:327`; `FloorType` `1886`, `RoofType` `1944` | |
| Triangulation: ear clipping of one simple ring, no holes, no inner points, no constraints | `geom::triangulate`, `geom.rs:153` | not enough for this |
| Faces of an arrangement of segments | `geom::faces`, `geom.rs:263` | useful to check split lines |
| A prism between two planes, cut by sections | `Solid::Prism { ring, bottom, top }`, `view3d.rs:159` | used by walls, ramps, runs |
| IFC: a prism between two planes as a shell | `Step::prism` and `Step::shell`, `ifc.rs:409`, `456` | used by ramps and walls |
| Walls attached to a floor follow one plane over its outline | `Bound::of`, `walls.rs:443` | the roof branch above it already follows many planes |
| IFC import of a slab whose top isn't one plane | `import.rs:1642`, `top_of` `273` | left out ("its top isn't flat"), or read as the plane of its largest upward face |
| Revit import of a sloped or stepped floor | `crates/rvt/src/floors.rs:206` | comes in level, with a note |
| File format | `FORMAT = 11`, `model.rs:90` | |

**The key point:** roofs already prove the pipeline can carry a top made of several planes. The work is to give floors
(and flat roofs) a top made of triangles, then let each consumer read "a list of planar pieces" where it reads "one plane"
today.

## The approach: a top made of planar pieces

One new query gives every consumer what it needs:

```rust
/// A floor's top as planar pieces in plan, each with its plane: one piece for a level or sloped floor,
/// the triangles of its shape (coplanar neighbours merged) for a shaped one.
pub fn floor_faces(&self, f: &Floor) -> Vec<(Vec<P2>, walls::Plane)>
```

`floor_top` stays for the unshaped case and as the reference the point heights are measured from. `floor_slabs` is
rebuilt on `floor_faces`. For a roof, `roof_faces` gains the same branch for a shaped flat roof, so `roof_pieces`,
`roof_slabs` and everything downstream work as they do for slopes.

### Data

```rust
/// Points and split lines on a floor's or a flat roof's top (IDEAS MOD-16).
pub struct Shape {
    pub points: Vec<ShapePoint>,
    pub lines: Vec<SplitLine>,
}

/// A point on the top, `z` mm above (negative: below) where the top would be without the shape.
pub struct ShapePoint { pub id: Id, pub guid: Guid, pub at: P2, pub z: f64 }

/// A crease the top folds along, between two of the shape's points or outline corners.
pub struct SplitLine { pub id: Id, pub guid: Guid, pub a: P2, pub b: P2 }
```

- `Floor` and `Roof` get `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Shape::is_empty")] pub shape: Shape`.
- `ShapePoint` and `SplitLine` are **parts** (`HasPart`, listed in `parts_now`, `sync_parts`, `forget_parts`), as sketch
  lines are, so a schedule, an agent or a later "edit this point" can name one by id.
- Heights are **relative** to the unshaped top, so changing the floor's `offset` moves the whole shape with it. Commands
  may take `absolute: true` and convert when they run.
- A corner of the outline (or of an opening) not listed among the points is at 0. A point may lie on an outline edge,
  where it adds a corner.
- Every end of a split line is one of the points or an outline corner. A command that adds a line with a loose end adds
  that end as a point, at the height the top has there at the time.
- `Layer` gets `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Not::not")] pub variable: bool`.
- **File format 13** (upstream's 12 came first), with a no-op step in `Model::migrate`. An older build that read a shaped floor would drop the shape
  and draw it flat. That's a misreading, not a field it can do without, so the bump is needed (CLAUDE.md, "A file is read
  kindly").

### Geometry

1. **Triangulate in plan:** a constrained Delaunay triangulation of the outline and its openings. The constraints are the
   outline edges, the opening edges and the split lines; the points are the inner vertices. Delaunay makes the result
   deterministic: the same points always give the same creases. Ties between cocircular points are broken by the
   corners' order, x and then y.
2. **Lift:** each vertex's z is the unshaped top there plus its point's `z`.
3. **Merge:** neighbouring triangles whose planes agree (within 0.01 mm at the shared vertices) merge into one polygon.
   A floor with points all at 0 is still one piece, and plans and IFC don't fill with needless diagonals.
4. **Thickness is plumb** for a shaped element: the type's thickness measured vertically, not square to each facet.
   Facets of different pitch then meet without gaps or overlaps underneath. At drainage falls of 1–2 % the difference is
   under 0.03 %. Sloped floors without a shape keep today's rule.
5. **With a variable layer**, the bottom is flat: the unshaped top less the type's thickness. Layers above the variable
   one follow the top, layers below it follow the bottom, and the variable layer is whatever is left at each point. Each
   facet becomes a `Solid::Prism` between its top plane and the flat bottom, not a `Solid::Slab` with a uniform rise.
6. **Caps:** `MAX_SHAPE_POINTS` (2,000) and `MAX_SPLIT_LINES` (2,000); every `z` within `MAX_COORD`. A triangulation
   past the cap is refused with the count, never truncated.

**The triangulation (built, phase 0).** The codebase writes its own geometry (the straight skeleton, the sketch solver,
CSG), its lints forbid panics, and the 3D view and plans run outside `Session::execute`'s `catch_unwind`, so a panic in
a dependency there would take the window down. So it is written here rather than taken from a crate such as `spade`:
`triangulation::constrained(outline, holes, points, lines)`, about 500 lines and 350 of tests.

- **Corners:** those within `TOL` of each other become one, the first in order of x and then y. An edge is cut at any
  corner within `TOL` of it, so a point on the outline bends it there.
- **Exact:** whether a corner lies left of a line, or inside a circle, is worked out in whole numbers on a 0.01 mm grid
  (`i128`), so a nearly flat triangle can't come out the wrong way round. That bounds a region to `MAX_ACROSS`, 10 km,
  well inside the 19 km where the in-circle sum would no longer fit.
- **Steps:** a sweep west to east triangulates the corners' convex hull; Lawson's flips make it Delaunay; Sloan's flips
  bring in each missing edge of the outline, the holes and the lines; Lawson's flips again, never across those edges; and
  a walk in from the hull, changing between outside and inside at each outline or hole edge, keeps the region's
  triangles.
- **Same answer in any order:** the output's corners and triangles are in a fixed order, so the same input in any
  order, either way round, gives an equal `Triangulation`.
- **Refused, saying why:** more than `MAX_CORNERS` (20,000) corners; a point not finite or past `MAX_COORD`; a region
  more than 10 km across; an outline or a hole with no area; a hole outside the outline or over another; a point or a
  line outside the outline or in a hole; a line shorter than a millimetre; edges that cross. Past 20 million flips it
  gives up rather than hold a command.
- **Speed:** 2,000 points with two lines in an L with a hole: about 17 ms, in the test build (the core is optimised
  there too).
- **Tests:** in the module. A random sweep of 400 cases, at least 100 of which must come out, checks that every triangle
  turns counter-clockwise, that they cover the region, and that no edge crosses a line. Leaving out the last Lawson pass
  or Sloan's flips each fails tests.

## Commands

The ids follow the established tool names, as the codebase does elsewhere.

| Command | Params | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `edit_shape` | `{id, points?: [{at, z, id?}], lines?: [{a, b, id?}], absolute?}` | Replaces the shape all at once, as `edit_boundary` does a sketch: what is sent back with an `id` keeps it. Without `points` or `lines`, it replies with the shape as it is: the points, including the corners with their heights; the split lines; the generated creases; and the pieces with their planes. That reply is what agents need to reason about falls. |
| `add_point` | `{id, at, z?, absolute?}` | One point; `z` defaults to the top's height there now (0 relative). |
| `add_split_line` | `{id, a, b}` | One line; loose ends become points at the current height. |
| `reset_shape` | `{id}` | Removes the shape. |
| `type` (floor, roof) | layers take `variable: true` | At most one per type; not on walls or ceilings. |
| `modify` (floor) | unchanged | Rejects `slope` or `arrow` on a shaped floor, with the reason (see Validation). |
| `falls` (phase 5) | `{id, drains: [[x, y], …], fall: 1.5, ridges?: [[[x, y], [x, y]], …]}` | Better than the established tools: sets point heights so water runs to the drains at no less than `fall` %, adding split lines along the valleys. Agents and architects describe a terrace this way, not point by point. |

Every reply lists the pieces' count and the lowest and highest point of the top. `inspect` on a floor already reports
`top: [lo, hi]` (`commands.rs:2122`); it must take the shape's points into account, not only the outline's.

## Validation (`Model::check`)

New rules, each with an error that says what to fix:

- A point outside the outline, or inside an opening: "point 100231 at (12500, 3400) is outside floor 100190: move it inside, or delete it".
- A split line that crosses another, crosses an opening, or leaves the outline (reuse `sketch::solve`'s problem kinds and wording).
- A split line end that is neither a point nor an outline corner.
- Two points within 1 mm of each other.
- A shape on a sloped floor (with `arrow`), or on a roof that isn't by footprint with `slope` 0. In version 1 the two are
  exclusive: shape a level element, and give its slope through the points.
- More than one variable layer in a type.
- **A variable layer thinner than nothing** anywhere: "at point 100231 the screed would be −12 mm: raise the point by 12
  mm or thicken the variable layer".
- With no variable layer, nothing bounds the depth: the slab just follows the top.

## What changes, consumer by consumer

| Consumer | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `Model::floor_slabs` (`model.rs:3755`) | one plane over the outline less openings | built on `floor_faces`; each piece less the openings |
| `Model::roof_faces` (`model.rs:3575`) | a flat roof is one plane | a shaped flat roof returns its pieces; `roof_rise` is plumb for them |
| 3D solids (`view3d.rs:511`, `612`) | `Solid::Slab` per piece | the same for constant thickness; `Solid::Prism` (top facet, flat bottom) with a variable layer |
| 3D layers (`view3d::layered`, `view3d.rs:741`) | a slab's layers in proportion; the `Prism` branch is walls only | a slab `Prism` branch: layers above the variable one from the top, below it from the bottom |
| Section layers (`render.rs:1230`) | each cut quad split in proportion to the layers' thicknesses | the same rule as 3D: fixed layers measured from the top or the bottom edge, the variable one between |
| Plan (`render.rs:1585`) | outline, openings, surface pattern, slope arrow | the pattern over each piece; split lines solid and generated creases dashed, thin, when the element is selected or being edited; each point's height as a label while editing (built as the desktop's overlay, not in `render.rs`, so it never prints) |
| Attached walls (`walls.rs:454`) | one plane over the floor's convex pieces | each piece with its own plane, as the roof branch above it does |
| Shafts (`Model::less_shafts`, `model.rs:3773`) | per slab face | already per face: no change, but a test |
| Move, copy, rotate, mirror (`commands.rs:8236`) | outline, openings, arrow, pattern | the points' `at` and the lines' ends too; a mirror keeps the heights |
| `edit_boundary` | redraws the outline | keeps the points inside the new outline and its openings, cuts each split line where it leaves the outline or enters an opening (keeping the pieces inside), and puts a point at the height the top had at each new end and each new corner, so the top round a new hole or a moved edge stays as it was; the reply names what was `dropped`, `cut` and `added` (built; test `a_hole_cut_through_a_shape_*`) |
| A floor's details (`element_json`, `commands.rs:2122`) | area and top from the outline | top range over every point; a volume (`volume_m3`) for every floor |
| Reinforce (`reinforce.rs:409`) | bars from `floor_top` | with a variable layer above the structure, the structure is flat: bars from the flat bottom. Otherwise refuse in version 1, saying why |
| IFC export (`ifc.rs:658`) | level: an extruded profile; sloped: per-piece Breps; quantities only `Width` when sloped | a shaped slab is **one closed `IfcFacetedBrep`**: top facets, a flat or following bottom, and plumb sides, all planar. Write `NetVolume` and `GrossVolume` for sloped and shaped slabs too, from the prisms. |
| Snaps (`snap.rs:320`, `603`) | outline edges and corners | the shape's points and split lines too |
| IFC import (`import.rs:1642`) | a top that isn't one plane is left out or forced flat | phase 5: read the upward faces' vertices as points relative to the highest plane, and the creases as split lines |
| Revit import (`crates/rvt/src/floors.rs:206`) | sloped or stepped comes in level | out of scope: reading the slab's shape from `.rvt` is research under the provenance fence |
| `lenient.rs`, `Element::refs_mut`, `parts_now` | | the new fields and parts, as the rules require |

## Desktop (`crates/ui-egui`)

- With a floor, or a flat roof, selected: a **Shape Editing** panel in the contextual tab, next to Slope Arrow
  (`lib.rs:3783`), with Modify Sub Elements, Add Point, Add Split Line and Reset Shape.
- **Add Point:** click on the top. The Options Bar takes the height and an Absolute check box.
- **Add Split Line:** two clicks, snapping to points, corners and edges.
- **Modify Sub Elements:** click a point or an edge (an edge sets both its ends) and type its height. Points drag in plan
  with the usual grips; in the 3D view (`orbit.rs`) their grips, and the corners', drag heights up or down.
- Every action runs a command. The canvas holds no geometry of its own (CLAUDE.md, "The UI is thin").
- egui_kittest tests: place a point at a model point, type −30, and check the reply's top range and the plan's pixels.

## Out of scope

- A different slope on each roof edge (upstream issue #74), and slope arrows on roofs and ceilings: separate items.
- Shaped ceilings; curved (smooth) tops; "pick supports" from beams.
- Toposolids. This work is their engine, though: a toposolid is a floor-like element whose top is a shape, so site and
  paving reuse `Shape`, the triangulation and every consumer change above.
- Reading shaped floors from `.rvt`.

## Phases, sizes and the tests that open each

Sizes as the roadmap gives them, for one developer working with agents.

| Phase | Size | First failing tests |
|---|---|---|
| **0. Triangulation** in `triangulation.rs` (built) | M | A square with a centre point gives 4 triangles; a split line is always an edge; an opening stays empty; the same input in any order gives the same triangles; duplicates, collinear runs, points on edges and the cap never panic (a property sweep). |
| **1. Shape on floors** (built, but for what the status above lists): data, commands, `check`, `floor_faces`, 3D, plan, sections (no variable layer), attached walls, transforms, `edit_boundary`, `inspect`, IFC export, snaps, format 13 | L | A 10 × 10 m floor with a drain at −30 mm gives 4 faces and the volume to 0.1 %; a section through the drain shows a V top; a wall attached under it follows the creases; IfcOpenShell validates the closed Brep with `express_rules=True`; mirror and move keep the shape; a format-12 file opens and a format-13 file is refused by 12; `hostile_params_never_panic_or_break_the_model` covers the new commands as it does every command. |
| **2. Variable layer** | M | A tile, screed (variable), membrane and concrete type: the section shows the concrete flat and the screed tapering; the 3D view's layers match; `check` refuses a point that makes the screed negative; reinforcement follows the flat structure. |
| **3. Desktop** | M | Add Point at a clicked model point with −30 typed; Add Split Line snapping to two corners; Reset Shape; the three looks screenshotted as `docs/areas/looking-at-results.md` asks. |
| **4. Flat roofs** | S | A flat roof by footprint with four drains; walls attached to it; a sloped roof refuses a shape. |
| **5. Extras**: `falls`, IFC import of multi-plane slabs, a spot slope annotation | M | `falls` with two drains gives at least 1.5 % everywhere and every point running to a drain; a shaped slab exported and imported comes back with the same points. |

**About two months in all.** After phases 0–2 (about a month) agents, the CLI and MCP can model falls to drains and
tapering screeds, and IFC carries them. The desktop tools follow.

## Open questions

1. Triangulation: written here (done in phase 0, in its own module rather than `geom`), unless the maintainer would
   rather have `spade`; #183 asks.
2. Shaped thickness plumb (proposed), or square to each facet as sloped floors are today?
3. Shape and slope arrow exclusive in version 1 (proposed), or a shape on top of a sloped plane?
4. Creases: plans draw every plane's edges always, as thin as the outline (built that way, as the simplest start).
   Generated creases dashed apart from the user's split lines, or shown only while selected, could come with the
   desktop tools.
5. Upstream first: IDEAS asks for an issue naming **MOD-16** before the work starts, so the fork doesn't drift from
   `IPedrax/BIMCraft`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run each line of a file (or args) as its own `run --cmd` on a fresh project (with -f files
copied, and -p prefix commands run first), printing the reply or error of the last command.
usage: each.py [-m] [-p prefixfile] [-f file] lines...  (or -i file of lines)
"""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aa380c34464cd9919/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
args = sys.argv[1:]
exe = ORIG
prefix = ''
files = []
lines = []
both = False
while args:
    a = args.pop(0)
    if a == '-m': exe = MINE
    elif a == '-b': both = True
    elif a == '-p': prefix = open(args.pop(0)).read()
    elif a == '-P': prefix += args.pop(0) + '\n'
    elif a == '-f': files.append(args.pop(0))
    elif a == '-i': lines += [l for l in open(args.pop(0)).read().split('\n') if l.strip()]
    else: lines.append(a)
def run(exe, line):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='e')
    for f in files:
        shutil.copy(f, d)
    open(os.path.join(d, 's.txt'), 'w').write(prefix + line + '\n')
    cmd = [exe, 'run'] + [os.path.basename(f) for f in files if f.endswith('.bimcraft')] + ['--script', 's.txt']
    p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    out = p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')[-1] if p.stdout.strip() else ''
    err = p.stderr.decode().strip()
    return out if p.returncode == 0 else 'ERR ' + err
for l in lines:
    r = run(exe, l)
    if both:
        m = run(MINE, l)
        flag = 'SAME' if m == r else 'DIFF'
        print(f'{flag} {l}\n   O: {r}' + ('' if m == r else f'\n   M: {m}'))
    else:
        print(f'{l}\n   -> {r}')

import subprocess, sys, json, tempfile, os, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
cat = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] in ('door', 'window') else 'door'
cases = [
    ['J-09', 'J-10'], ['P1', 'P2'], ['P1', 'Q1'], ['P1', 'P1'], ['1', 'P1', 'P2'], ['P1', 'P2', '1', '2'],
    ['P2', 'P1'], ['P1', 'P3'], ['009'], ['P009', 'P010'], ['P1', 'P2', 'Q5', 'Q6'], ['Q5', 'Q6', 'P1', 'P2'],
    ['P1', 'P2', 'Q5', 'Q6', 'Q7'], ['A-1', 'A-2'], ['A 1', 'A 2'], ['1', '3'], ['P01', 'P02'], ['P9', 'P10'],
    ['P10', 'P9'], ['p1', 'P2'], ['1a', '2a'], ['P1', 'P2', 'X'], ['P1.5', 'P2.5'], ['ÁÉ1', 'ÁÉ2'],
    ['P1', 'P2', '5'], ['5', 'P1', 'P2'], ['P1', 'P2', 'Q1', 'Q2', '1', '2'],
]
def run(seeds):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    lines = ['wall {"points": [[0,0],[900000,0]]}']
    off = 1000
    for m in seeds:
        lines.append('%s {"wall": 100002, "offset": %d, "mark": %s}' % (cat, off, json.dumps(m)))
        off += 2000
    lines.append('%s {"wall": 100002, "offset": %d}' % (cat, off))
    lines.append('%s {"wall": 100002, "offset": %d}' % (cat, off + 2000))
    open(os.path.join(d, 's.txt'), 'w').write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
    p = subprocess.run([ORIG, 'run', '--script', 's.txt'], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    outs = p.stdout.decode().strip().split('\n')
    if p.returncode:
        return p.stderr.decode()
    return [json.loads(x)['mark'] for x in outs[-2:]]
for c in cases:
    print(c, '->', run(c))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""craft.py base.bimcraft 'python statements on d (the doc) and E (elements dict by int id)' [command]
Writes a crafted copy, opens it with the original (and mine with -b), runs a trivial command, prints the result."""
import json, sys, subprocess, tempfile, os, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-aa380c34464cd9919/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
args = sys.argv[1:]
both = False
if args and args[0] == '-b':
    both = True
    args = args[1:]
base, code = args[0], args[1]
cmd = args[2] if len(args) > 2 else 'level {"elevation": 90000}'
d = json.load(open(base))
E = {int(k): v for k, v in d['elements'].items()}
def guid(i):
    return E[i]['guid']
exec(code)
d['elements'] = {str(k): v for k, v in sorted(E.items())}
def run(exe):
    t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    json.dump(d, open(os.path.join(t, 'c.bimcraft'), 'w'), indent=2)
    p = subprocess.run([exe, 'run', 'c.bimcraft', '--cmd', cmd], cwd=t, capture_output=True)
    shutil.rmtree(t)
    return (p.stdout.decode() + p.stderr.decode()).strip()
o = run(ORIG)
print('O:', o)
if both:
    m = run(MINE)
    print('M:', m)
    print('SAME' if m == o else 'DIFF')

import math
a=(0.0,0.0); b=(9000.0,0.0); deg=30.0
targets = {(5500,-550): 5553.156351417149, (7500,-300): 7572.380224404302}
sw = math.radians(deg); c = math.hypot(b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1]); half = sw/2
r = c/2/abs(math.sin(half)); dd = c/2/math.tan(half)
ux, uy = (b[0]-a[0])/c, (b[1]-a[1])/c
cx, cy = (a[0]+b[0])/2 - uy*dd, (a[1]+b[1])/2 + ux*dd
a0 = math.atan2(a[1]-cy, a[0]-cx)
print('centre', cx, cy, r, a0)
for p, t in targets.items():
    ang = math.atan2(p[1]-cy, p[0]-cx)
    cands = {}
    da = ang - a0
    cands['r*da'] = r*da
    cands['da*r'] = da*r
    cands['r*(da mod)'] = r*((da) % (2*math.pi))
    # fraction of sweep * length
    L = r*sw
    cands['da/sw*L'] = da/sw*L
    cands['(da/sw)*L'] = (da/sw)*L
    cands['L*(da/sw)'] = L*(da/sw)
    # via vector angle between start vector and point vector
    v0 = (a[0]-cx, a[1]-cy); v1 = (p[0]-cx, p[1]-cy)
    ang2 = math.atan2(v0[0]*v1[1]-v0[1]*v1[0], v0[0]*v1[0]+v0[1]*v1[1])
    cands['r*atan2(cross,dot)'] = r*ang2
    # centre line radius (shift 150 to the right: arc ccw -> right is away from centre)
    for name, rr in (('rc+150', r+150), ('rc-150', r-150)):
        cands[name+' da'] = rr*da
    for k, v in cands.items():
        print(p, k, repr(v), 'MATCH' if v == t else '')
EOF

a=(0.0,0.0); b=(9000.0,0.0); deg=30.0
targets = {(5500,-550): 5553.156351417149, (7500,-300): 7572.380224404302, (1500,-300): 1531.2562149428609,

sw = math.radians(deg); c = 9000.0; half = sw/2
r = c/2/abs(math.sin(half)); dd = c/2/math.tan(half)
cx, cy = 4500.0, dd
a0 = math.atan2(a[1]-cy, a[0]-cx)
L = r*sw
co, si = math.cos(a0), math.sin(a0)
v0x, v0y = a[0]-cx, a[1]-cy
cnt = {}
for p, t in targets.items():
    dx, dy = p[0]-cx, p[1]-cy
    cands = {}
    lx, ly = dx*co + dy*si, -dx*si + dy*co
    g = math.atan2(ly, lx)
    cands['rot'] = g/sw*L

    # normalized start vector

    lx2, ly2 = dx*ux + dy*uy, -dx*uy + dy*ux

    cands['rotn'] = g2/sw*L
    cands['rotn_r'] = g2*r
    # chord tangent frame
    for k, v in cands.items():
        cnt.setdefault(k, 0)

 'a0+sw*i/n': lambda i: a0 + sw*i/n,

a=(0.0,0.0); b=(8000.0,0.0); deg=90.0; n=42
T = {8: (1737.8691028887642, -1184.8590920423972), 9: (1933.3190737990599, -1265.817120758869), 39: (7847.638042048293, -146.767596258896),

sw = math.radians(deg); c = 8000.0; half = sw/2
r = c/2/abs(math.sin(half)); dd = c/2/math.tan(half)
cx, cy = 4000.0, dd
a0 = math.atan2(a[1]-cy, a[0]-cx)
a1 = math.atan2(b[1]-cy, b[0]-cx)
forms = {
 'a0+sw*i/n': lambda i: a0 + sw*i/n,
 'a0+i*(sw/n)': lambda i: a0 + i*(sw/n),
 'a0+sw*(i/n)': lambda i: a0 + sw*(i/n),
 'a0*(1-t)+a1*t': lambda i: a0*(1-i/n) + a1*(i/n),
 'a0+(a1-a0)*t': lambda i: a0 + (a1-a0)*(i/n),
 'a0+(a1-a0)*i/n': lambda i: a0 + (a1-a0)*i/n,
 'a0+t*sw': lambda i: a0 + (i/n)*sw,
}
step = sw/n
acc = [a0]
for i in range(n): acc.append(acc[-1] + step)
forms['accum'] = lambda i: acc[i]
for name, f in forms.items():
    ok = 0
    for i, t in T.items():
        ang = f(i)
        p = (cx + r*math.cos(ang), cy + r*math.sin(ang))
        if p == t: ok += 1
    print(name, ok, '/', len(T))

v = (a[0]-cx, a[1]-cy)
ok = 0

    th = sw*i/n
    p = (cx + v[0]*math.cos(th) - v[1]*math.sin(th), cy + v[0]*math.sin(th) + v[1]*math.cos(th))
    if p == t: ok += 1

# incremental rotation

    pts.append((x*co - y*si, x*si + y*co))

import math
cases = [((0.0,0.0),(1000.0,0.0),(300.0,-400.0),165.7499673021964), ((0.0,0.0),(1000.0,0.0),(123.4,-321.9),178.37936904779554),
